control_failures.control_label: atmospheric gas testing before and during hot work

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: unplanned release of chemical energy at PSV-7103

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control GAS_TEST_BEFORE_AND_DURING_HOT_WORK: the atmospheric gas testing before and during hot work was not in place, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as an organisational factor.

recommendations: Restore the atmospheric gas testing before and during hot work on PSV-7103 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining hazardous-area electrical equipment, specifically inspecting Ex equipment and enclosures. PSV-7103 (tank relief and vent devices) is in service for tank overpressure and vacuum protection. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the atmospheric gas testing before and during hot work was not in place. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 28 February 2025 a high potential incident was recorded on PSV-7103 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a planned shutdown; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
